solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrive before loud noise envelops a stand-up performer?

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next in the answer

parts.note: to arrive is to come

indicators.note: envelops means the noise word wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone who turns up just as a racket surrounds them on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic who performs on their feet in front of a crowd is a stand-up; the question mark flags this is one kind.

clue.text: Taking everything outside, chill another excellent wine

indicators.note: the outside letters of every one of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone chilling yet another bottle of fine wine, taking all the gear outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking everything outside' takes the first and last letters of chill, another and excellent: CL, AR, ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Monitoring body observe, follow closely

parts.note: to observe is to watch
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A description of what a regulator does: keeps an eye on things and tails suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator that keeps an eye on an industry or the authorities is called this.

clue.text: Not finishing publisher's book info that's obscure

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a blurb is the publisher's promotional description on a book's jacket

explanation.surface: A jacket description left unfinished, so its information stays unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to make it indistinct, to smear or cloud it.

clue.text: Grow tired over large bottle of cider?

parts.note: to flag is to grow tired
over can mean on, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A drinker getting weary over a big jug of cider.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or bottle, traditionally for cider or wine; the question mark marks cider as an example.

clue.text: Give notice of conflict over ending of immigration

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a war is a conflict

indicators.note: ending of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A political warning that a fight is brewing over stopping immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone beforehand of danger is to give them notice of it.

clue.text: Counter the effect of thin metal sword

definitions.meaning: to thwart or frustrate a plan
metal beaten into a thin sheet, as used in the kitchen

explanation.surface: A fencer neutralising an attack with a slender metal blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: thwarting a plan, metal sheeting for wrapping, and a fencing weapon.

clue.text: Odd call before tragic king gives signal to come out of hiding

definitions.text: signal to come out of hiding

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
odd suggests the letters of the word that follows are out of their usual order

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A strange summons before a doomed monarch signals people may emerge from cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges CALL to ALLC, ahead of LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The siren after an air raid told people it was safe to leave shelters.

clue.text: Encountered core of brick sized in centimetres, perhaps

parts.note: encountered means met

indicators.note: core of picks the central letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone meeting a brick measured in centimetres rather than inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Measurements given in centimetres belong to the decimal measuring system based on the metre.

clue.text: Violently angry when alcohol is used in student charity raiser

indicators.note: is used in tells us the drink goes inside the event word

parts.note: rag week is a British student fundraising event for charity
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Fury when drink gets into a student fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British student charity event, often a week of stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious and out of control is in a rage, hence this adjective.

clue.text: Last of articles in illuminated catalogue

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other word

parts.note: illuminated means lit

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The final item of an illuminated manuscript's inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is an itemised record, a register of things one after another.

clue.text: Go off romantic meeting outside school

indicators.note: outside means the meeting word wraps around the school

parts.note: a date is a romantic meeting
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A couple leaving for a date outside the school gates.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that goes off explodes, which is to blow up.

clue.text: Regularly target a certain valuable object

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word that follows

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Advice to aim repeatedly at one particular prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of target: TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized possession of great worth, such as a precious heirloom.

clue.text: Hot and humid current crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the first word spans the other, holding it inside

parts.note: current affairs are topical

explanation.surface: A steamy flow passing over a river, as in a jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Equatorial climates are sultry, steamy and warm.

clue.text: Make complicated magical sign when lacking power

indicators.note: when lacking says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star used as a magic symbol

explanation.surface: A wizard's symbol that becomes confusing when it loses its force.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare or tangle up, making a situation knotty and involved.

clue.text: Do a bar when drunk overseas

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub crawl while drunk on holiday in a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a foreign country, across the sea, is being away from home.

clue.text: Put together game involving cues

definitions.meaning: to combine resources into a shared fund
a cue game played on a table with pockets, like billiards

explanation.surface: Players clubbing together for a cue sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: combining money or resources, and the pocket-table cue game.

clue.text: Equality one's found in Conservatives or Labour, say

indicators.note: found in places the numeral inside the political word

parts.note: the Conservatives and Labour are British political parties
one's reads as one is; one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A claim that fairness exists within one of the big British political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level or equal in status or value.

clue.text: Vegetable is to spoil, grown without its outer parts

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: without its outer parts drops the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener's lament that an overgrown vegetable spoils once it loses its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without its outer parts' strips grown to ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A large green gourd-like British vegetable, an overgrown courgette.

clue.text: Some Near Eastern region

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A territory somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone or district is a stretch of land.

clue.text: Breeze in between wife and daughter

indicators.note: between places the word in amid the two abbreviations

explanation.surface: A light breeze blowing between a wife and her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a gentle current of moving air.

clue.text: Labour wants second rail service

parts.note: a train is a rail service

explanation.surface: The Labour Party wanting a second railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it is the verb meaning to work hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself hard, to toil and struggle.

clue.text: Keep the queen's long-term servant

parts.note: to keep is to retain
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: Keeping a royal household's loyal old servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A family servant of many years' standing, in old-fashioned usage.

clue.text: Drink with male group of players

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Tea taken with a man in a sports side.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in a sport is made up of several competitors.
